name: Restaurant
blurb: Ordering, saying what you do not eat, waiting, paying.

items.en: A coffee and a cake, please.
items.ans: コーヒー|と|ケーキ|を|ください
alts: コーヒーとケーキをお願いします
items.note: と joins nouns as a complete list — coffee and cake, and nothing else implied. It never joins whole sentences the way English 'and' does.
も replaces は or を rather than joining them: これも, never これをも. It carries the 'too' on its own.
ません is the negative of ます on the same stem: 食べ + ません. は marks 肉 as the topic, which is how a standing preference is stated rather than a one-off refusal.

items.ans: 何時|から|開いて|います|か
items.note: から marks the starting point — open from what time. It is a separate tile from 何時, and swapping it for まで would ask when you close. 開いて + います is the state the shop is in, not an action it is performing.
注文 is a noun, and し + ました makes it a verb: 'did ordering'. Any する noun works this way. ました is the past of ます on the same stem.
The te-form plus います is an action in progress. ている is the same pattern spoken plainly; います is the polite one, and the bank offers both.

items.ans: お会計|を|お願いします
items.note: The same frame as ordering: Ｘをお願いします. Only the noun changes, which is what makes it worth learning as one shape.
